text:
maria: FYI seeing eviction oscillation in kv cache on 2p/4g serving nodes when clients send long-context streams (~20k tokens). Memory climbs then drops repeatedly and latency spikes.

devon: Can you share which model and kernel config? :eyes:

maria: host/model: rw-vicuna-13b-quant; kernel: auto-select with int8 path. Repro on canary. Quick trace:

```
AllocLive: +2.3G -> +3.9G over 30s
pprof heap: inuse_objects: 1.2M
hot pages: kvpage-123, kvpage-458
stack: runtime/kv/cache.go:287
```

jules: Interesting. Any eviction logs? We saw repeated evict->prefetch loops earlier with fragmented keysets.

maria: logs show alternating evict of cohort A then a prefetch burst for same prefixes seconds later. eviction_reason=frag_threshold and then prefetch due to miss ratio > 0.8

hao: My suspicion: the cache key design couples session-id + prefix-hash. Longctx requests keep creating unique session fingerprints (differs per request slice) so same logical prefix maps to different keys across requests. That fragments residency and causes churn.

perf-engineer: We profiled pagefaults — page scan time correlated with longctx. microbench:

```
probe: cache_get: 1.8us -> 5.4us under churn
pagefaults/sec: 240 -> 1900
KV resident pages: 2.1G -> 4.4G
```

liz: Are TTLs super short? If keys expire aggressively, repeated re-inserts would explain the oscillation.

maria: TTL currently 30s for session keys. But even increasing TTL to 2m didn't fully stabilize; we still see fragmentation due to key divergence.

devon: Could we canonicalize keying so prefix-only keys for shared sequences, and keep session-anchored keys for ephemeral tokens? Maybe a two-tier hash: prefix-id + session-salt optional.

hao: Agreed. We tried a lease-based approach in a branch: if prefix fingerprint matches existing canonical key within X ms, reuse canonical ID instead of creating new session-fingerprint. Early eval reduced misses by ~45% in synthetic workload.

jules: Did that change affect isolation? Need to ensure tenant/session isolation for security.

hao: Isolation preserved — lease binds to tenant scope, not session. Only merges identical prefix fingerprints within same tenant.

maria: Quick experiment results on canary: with lease+ttl-smoothing we saw memory plateau instead of oscillation. Latency p50 down 12%, p95 down 26% for longctx traces.

prod-observability: Observability note — add a per-prefix residency gauge and eviction counter tag (reason=frag_threshold|ttl_expiry|memory_pressure). Current metrics are too coarse.

perf-engineer: Agree. Also add sampling for prefix fingerprint entropy to detect divergence patterns.

devon: Action items:
- hao: push lease-key prototype PR and tests (owner)
- jules: add residency and eviction-reason metrics + dashboard (owner)
- maria: run 24h canary with 10% traffic and report
- liz: validate no tenant isolation regressions

liz: timeline?

maria: PRs by EOD, canary tomorrow morning, will post followups here.

sre-bot: deploy-canary started: canary-id=canary-2026-03-19-01

devon: Awesome. If we still see oscillation after lease keys, next step is compaction pass that coalesces keys with short-lived diffs.

maria: Thanks all. If you want raw traces I uploaded pprof + heap dumps to s3: s3://redwood-ops/tmp/maria/evict-osc-1768702468/

hao: I'll take a look tonight. :coffee:

jules: Good thread. Will follow up once metrics are added. :thumbsup:
